shared_ancestry_policy: FRANK->ClayCode restatements are not independent confirmation

reviews.frank_statement: FRANK should be treated as a hierarchical/multiscale loop-of-loops whose loop identity, timescale, coupling and continue/halt state are observable and controllable.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Those dimensions are merely host scheduler metadata and can be erased from ClayCode semantic identity without changing behavior.
reviews.falsifier: Matched programs with different declared timescale/commit/order/halting policies produce identical typed state traces across production H1/H2 fixtures, or a schedule-blind semantic hash remains collision-free under all behavior-changing mutations.
independent_checks: Current-run 2,000-case synthetic scheduler discriminator: flattening 1:2:5 timescales changed 2,000/2,000 endpoints and reversing sequential order changed 2,000/2,000 endpoints; schedule-blind identity collapsed four behaviorally distinct variants into one.
Lingua Franca primary documentation independently treats logical time, timers, deterministic same-tag ordering and feedback causality as program semantics.
MLIR SCF primary documentation independently carries loop state and explicit continuation conditions in structured IR.
adversarial_checks: Snapshot-atomic same-epoch loop declarations were permuted; observable endpoint and canonical semantic trace hash changed 0/2,000, showing not every source ordering dimension is semantic.
reviews.reason: The semantic need survives, but it should be a generic typed scheduler/recurrence contract, not a FRANK-specific cognitive primitive or new reader syntax.
reviews.claycode_action: Preserve timescale/clock, commit model, semantically ordered sequencing and recurrence policy in typed IR/runtime identity; canonicalize order only where the type declares same-epoch snapshot/set semantics.

reviews.frank_statement: Adaptive recurrence/halting should be available because too much recurrence can waste compute or degrade useful behavior.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A fixed recurrence budget is simpler and sufficient; adaptive halting adds unstable policy state without meaningful benefit.
reviews.falsifier: On matched H1/H2 replay workloads, adaptive policies fail to reduce cost at matched semantics/quality or cause higher false-halt/recovery cost than fixed budgets.
independent_checks: Current-run synthetic comparison saved a mean 10.44% recurrence count versus fixed-5 while endpoint differences remained small in this toy; 1,260/2,000 endpoints were nevertheless non-identical, so policy cannot be hidden from receipts/identity when behavior matters.
Kohli et al. 2026 independently report that extra recurrent depth can extend reasoning depth but excessive recurrence can produce overthinking.
adversarial_checks: The current-run savings are proxy-only and do not establish task quality; no FRANK runtime or H1 workload was executed.
reviews.reason: ClayCode needs to represent recurrence budget and halt/continue policy plus receipts, but no particular adaptive controller is promoted.
reviews.claycode_action: Make halting/budget policy explicit in typed runtime semantics and benchmark fixed vs adaptive policies later on frozen H1 traces.

reviews.frank_statement: Loop dynamics readouts may classify convergence, productive bounded cycles, stalled and unstable regimes.
reviews.counterhypothesis: These categories are useful diagnostics only and do not belong in core language semantics; generic measurement records are sufficient.
reviews.falsifier: A production FRANK/H1 counterexample requires a new primitive because generic records, typed enums, epochs, provenance and measurement receipts cannot represent the needed readout or intervention.
independent_checks: Concurrent ClayCode loop-runtime and loop-network executable probes represented stalled/diverging/productive-cycle distinctions without a new core primitive.
Current GWT/Hyperposition contracts already require typed recurrence/cross-timescale/readout fields and intervention receipts.
adversarial_checks: No live FRANK loop classifier was tested; recurrence metrics remain non-authoritative and are not emergence evidence.
reviews.reason: Retain the readout concept as typed library/runtime measurement structures, not a special syntax or truth-bearing primitive.
reviews.claycode_action: Use generic typed measurement/readout records with provenance and intervention refs; keep recurrence != emergence and readout != authority.
